import Mathlib

inductive BinarySearchTree : Type
| Empty : BinarySearchTree
| Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree
deriving Inhabited

def view (t : BinarySearchTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => ∅
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_bst (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => True
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

def get_left (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ l _ => some l
  | _ => none

def get_right (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ r => some r
  | _ => none

def get_val (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v _ _ => some v
  | _ => none

def BinarySearchTree.is_node (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ _ => True
  | _ => False

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zigzag_precond (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_bst t ∧ 
  BinarySearchTree.is_node t ∧ 
  (match get_left t with 
   | some p => BinarySearchTree.is_node p ∧ 
               (match get_right p with 
                | some x => BinarySearchTree.is_node x 
                | none => False)
   | none => False)
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def zigzag (t : BinarySearchTree) 
    (h_precond : zigzag_precond t) : BinarySearchTree :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node g (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr)) gr =>
      BinarySearchTree.Node x (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl xl) (BinarySearchTree.Node g xr gr)
  | _ => t
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zigzag_postcond (t : BinarySearchTree) (result : BinarySearchTree)
    (_ : zigzag_precond t) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_bst result ∧
  view result = view t ∧
  -- Structural properties: X (grandchild, originally P's right child) is now root
  get_val result = get_val (get_right (get_left t).get!).get!
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem zigzag_postcond_satisfied (t : BinarySearchTree)
    (h_precond : zigzag_precond t) :
    zigzag_postcond t (zigzag t h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  have hview : ∀ (v : Int) (l r : BinarySearchTree),
      view (BinarySearchTree.Node v l r) = view l ∪ view r ∪ {v} := by
    intro v l r
    simp [view]
  rcases t with _ | ⟨g, l, gr⟩
  · exact (show False from h_precond.2.1).elim
  · rcases l with _ | ⟨p, pl, pr⟩
    · exact (show False ∧ False from h_precond.2.2).1.elim
    · rcases pr with _ | ⟨x, xl, xr⟩
      · exact (show True ∧ False from h_precond.2.2).2.elim
      · -- main case
        have hbst : (∀ y ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl
                        (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr)), y < g) ∧
            is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr)) ∧
            (∀ y ∈ view gr, y > g) ∧ is_bst gr := h_precond.1
        have hinner : (∀ y ∈ view pl, y < p) ∧ is_bst pl ∧
            (∀ y ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr), y > p) ∧
            is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr) := hbst.2.1
        have hx : (∀ y ∈ view xl, y < x) ∧ is_bst xl ∧
            (∀ y ∈ view xr, y > x) ∧ is_bst xr := hinner.2.2.2
        -- membership helpers
        have mxl : ∀ y ∈ view xl, y ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr) := by
          intro y hy
          rw [hview]
          exact Set.mem_union_left _ (Set.mem_union_left _ hy)
        have mxr : ∀ y ∈ view xr, y ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr) := by
          intro y hy
          rw [hview]
          exact Set.mem_union_left _ (Set.mem_union_right _ hy)
        have mxx : x ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr) := by
          rw [hview]
          exact Set.mem_union_right _ rfl
        have mI : ∀ y ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr),
            y ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr)) := by
          intro y hy
          rw [hview]
          exact Set.mem_union_left _ (Set.mem_union_right _ hy)
        have hpx : p < x := hinner.2.2.1 x mxx
        have hxg : x < g := hbst.1 x (mI x mxx)
        have hL : is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl xl) := by
          show (∀ y ∈ view pl, y < p) ∧ is_bst pl ∧
            (∀ y ∈ view xl, y > p) ∧ is_bst xl
          exact ⟨hinner.1, hinner.2.1, fun y hy => hinner.2.2.1 y (mxl y hy), hx.2.1⟩
        have hR : is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node g xr gr) := by
          show (∀ y ∈ view xr, y < g) ∧ is_bst xr ∧
            (∀ y ∈ view gr, y > g) ∧ is_bst gr
          exact ⟨fun y hy => hbst.1 y (mI y (mxr y hy)), hx.2.2.2, hbst.2.2.1, hbst.2.2.2⟩
        refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
        · show is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node x (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl xl)
              (BinarySearchTree.Node g xr gr))
          show (∀ y ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl xl), y < x) ∧
              is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl xl) ∧
              (∀ y ∈ view (BinarySearchTree.Node g xr gr), y > x) ∧
              is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node g xr gr)
          refine ⟨?_, hL, ?_, hR⟩
          · intro y hy
            rw [hview] at hy
            simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hy
            rcases hy with (h | h) | h
            · exact lt_trans (hinner.1 y h) hpx
            · exact hx.1 y h
            · rw [h]; exact hpx
          · intro y hy
            rw [hview] at hy
            simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hy
            rcases hy with (h | h) | h
            · exact hx.2.2.1 y h
            · exact lt_trans hxg (hbst.2.2.1 y h)
            · rw [h]; exact hxg
        · show view (BinarySearchTree.Node x (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl xl)
              (BinarySearchTree.Node g xr gr))
              = view (BinarySearchTree.Node g
                  (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr)) gr)
          ext y
          simp only [hview, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
          tauto
        · show get_val (BinarySearchTree.Node x (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl xl)
              (BinarySearchTree.Node g xr gr))
              = get_val (get_right (get_left (BinarySearchTree.Node g
                  (BinarySearchTree.Node p pl (BinarySearchTree.Node x xl xr)) gr)).get!).get!
          rfl
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## Analysis

**The operation.** The precondition guarantees the tree has shape
```
t = Node g (Node p pl (Node x xl xr)) gr
```
i.e. `G` has left child `P`, and `P` has right child `X`. The Zig-Zag (left–right rotation) produces

```
result = Node x (Node p pl xl) (Node g xr gr)
```

**Set preservation.** Both trees have view `view pl ∪ view xl ∪ view xr ∪ view gr ∪ {p,x,g}`, so the equality is pure set algebra (`ext` + `tauto`).

**BST preservation.** From `is_bst t` we get:
* `pl < p`, `p < view(Node x xl xr)` (so `p < x`, `p < xl`), `xl < x < xr`, everything in the left subtree `< g`, `gr > g`.

Hence for the result:
* left child `Node p pl xl`: `pl < p`, `xl > p`, both BSTs ✔
* right child `Node g xr gr`: `xr < g`, `gr > g`, both BSTs ✔
* everything on the left of `x` (`pl < p < x`, `xl < x`, `p < x`) is `< x` ✔
* everything on the right of `x` (`xr > x`, `g > x`, `gr > g > x`) is `> x` ✔

**Structure.** `get_val result = some x = get_val (get_right (get_left t).get!).get!` holds by `rfl`.

For the degenerate shapes, the precondition reduces definitionally to `False`, which I extract via type ascriptions (`show False ∧ False from …`) to avoid fragile projections.

analysis:
The student’s implementation does match the required Zig-Zag / left-right rotation shape.

What the natural language requires:
- A Zig-Zag where:
  - `G` is the root,
  - `P` is the left child of `G`,
  - `X` is the right child of `P`.
- After rotation:
  - `X` becomes the new root,
  - `P` becomes the left child of `X`,
  - `G` becomes the right child of `X`.
- Also prove set preservation and BST preservation.

What the student implemented:
- In `zigzag`, the only active case is:
  - `Node g (Node p pl (Node x xl xr)) gr`
- It returns:
  - `Node x (Node p pl xl) (Node g xr gr)`

This is exactly the standard left-right (zig-zag) rotation:
- original:
  - `G`
    - left = `P`
      - left = `pl`
      - right = `X`
        - left = `xl`
        - right = `xr`
    - right = `gr`
- result:
  - `X`
    - left = `P`
      - left = `pl`
      - right = `xl`
    - right = `G`
      - left = `xr`
      - right = `gr`

So structurally, this is the correct algorithm.
